Definition: an endomap is dagger-self-adjoint when f dag = f. Verbatim.
Definition: f is dagger-positive when f = g dag after g for some map g. Lean's f = g >> dag g is exactly (dag g) after g with g : X to Y existentially bound over Y, matching "for some other map g".

Definition (eff.tex 2150.10). Field by field: clause 1 is daggerCat (a DaggerCat on PureCat C) plus dag_asrt (asrt_p dag = asrt_p) plus dag_diamond_adjoint (f is diamond-adjoint to f dag, i.e. diaPull f = diaPush (dag f), the 206II.1 relation in the right order); clause 2 is sqrt_existsUnique (unique dagger-positive square root of a dagger-positive map); clause 3 is diamond_pos_dagger_pos. Definition of a dagger-prime-effectus, i.e. 215V's name for the three axioms of Theorem 215III. All three match: (1) unique square root q with q & q = p for every predicate; (2) asrt_{p&q} squared = asrt_p asrt_q asrt_q asrt_p; (3) a quotient for a sharp predicate is a sharp map - Lean's quot_sharp quantifies over all quotients for sharp predicates, which is the point's "e.g. zeta_s" reading. 215VII's remarks (the fundamental formula of quadratic Jordan algebras, Selinger's unique-square-root axiom) are not rendered.

Theorem dagger-theorem: an andthen-effectus is a dagger-effectus iff it satisfies the three axioms. Stated as Nonempty (DaggerEffectus C) iff DaggerPrimeEffectus C, which is the right reading since a dagger-effectus is data. Proof is the thesis's: necessity 216XI, sufficiency 220II. Note the "with dagger as in 217II" clause is lost here too, inherited from dagger_thm_sufficiency.

Proof is the thesis's: axiom 2 gives the dagger-positive square root g = h dag after h, whose diamond-self-adjointness is the displayed four-step computation using that h is diamond-adjoint to h dag; the converse is axiom 3.

Lemma dagger-eff-square-root: every predicate has a unique square root. Proof is the thesis's, step for step - asrt_p is diamond-positive hence dagger-positive (ax. 3), take its dagger-positive square root f (ax. 2), f is diamond-positive by 216I so f = asrt_{1 after f}, q = 1 after f works, and uniqueness comes from andthen_square_rule plus ax. 2.

Proposition asrt-iso: asrt_p after alpha = alpha after asrt_{p after alpha} for an isomorphism alpha, in an andthen-effectus with square roots. The hypothesis is taken as an explicit existence-only hsqrt, which is what the phrase "with square roots" and the thesis's proof both use. Proof is the thesis's: alpha inv after asrt_q after alpha is diamond-self-adjoint by 209IV, its square is alpha inv after asrt_p after alpha, uniqueness of diamond-positive maps, then postcompose alpha.

The "in other words" half of diamond-adjunction: f_diamond is the left order-adjoint of f^box, f_diamond(s) <= t iff s <= f^box(t). Proof is the thesis's opening reformulation.
Exercise order-adj-basics clause 1: f_diamond is order preserving. Proof is bsols.tex:2966 clause 1, via the unit of the adjunction.

Exercise spred-sup: (xi^box after xi_diamond)(t) = s join t for sharp s, t and a quotient xi for s. Exercise exc-diamond-adj clause 1: f^diamond = g_diamond iff f_diamond = g^diamond. Stated as an iff. Local deviation from bsols.tex:3068: ours proves the key implication by a five-step chain of adjunction equivalences plus antisymmetry, where bsols uses the double-orthocomplement trick.

Clause 2: if f and g are diamond-adjoint then im f = ceil(1 after g). Proof is bsols' one line im f = f_diamond(1) = g^diamond(1) = ceil(1 after g), with pi_1 an isomorphism supplying f_diamond(1) = im f.
Exercise diamond-squares clause 1: the square of a diamond-self-adjoint map is diamond-self-adjoint. Proof is bsols.tex:3086 clause 1, via functoriality 207VI.
Clause 2: diamond-positive maps are diamond-self-adjoint. Proof is bsols' - unfold f = g after g and apply clause 1.
Clause 3: if f is diamond-positive and f after f is pure then f after f is diamond-positive. The purity hypothesis is the exercise's own. Proof is bsols'.

Lemma iso-diamond-adjoint clause 1: s after alpha is sharp for sharp s and an isomorphism alpha. Proof is the thesis's - exhibit s after alpha as the image of pi_s after alpha inv (helper isImage_compr_comp_inv, which reproduces the thesis's two-line verification).
Clause 2: alpha^diamond(s) = s after alpha and alpha_diamond(s) = s after alpha inv, so alpha and alpha inv are diamond-adjoint. All three conjuncts stated. Proof is the thesis's.
Definition sharp-map: f is a sharp map when s after f is sharp for every sharp s. Verbatim. 210III (in vNop the sharp maps are exactly the nmi-maps) is not formalized here.

Exercise sharp-ceil: f is sharp iff ceil(p after f) = ceil p after f for every predicate p. Stated as the iff the exercise asks for. Proof is bsols.tex:3104, using 203XIII ceiling-within-ceiling in one direction and instantiating at sharp p in the other.

Definition (eff.tex parsec 2110 point 20): an andthen-effectus is a diamond-effectus with (1) a unique diamond-positive asrt_p with 1 after asrt_p = p for every predicate, and (2) purity of every quotient-after-comprehension composite. Both axioms are fields and match. The Remarks 211III and 211IIIa (the assert intuition, polar decomposition) are prose and are not formalized; 211IV (vNop) lives in VNExamples.
The assert map asrt_p, obtained by unique choice from axiom 1. Matches the definition.

Definition of p andthen q = q after asrt_p (Lean asrt p >> q, i.e. q after asrt_p - the thesis's order, not the reverse). The abbreviation p squared = p andthen p is not introduced as a separate definition but is used inline.

Proposition sharp-prop: for a predicate p the three conditions "p is sharp", "p & p = p", "asrt_p after asrt_p = asrt_p" are equivalent. Rendered as two iffs with (1) as the hub, which is the same three-way equivalence. Proof is the thesis's throughout, including the (2) implies (1) argument through ceil p minus p and 208I, and the long (1) implies (3) argument through the second andthen-effectus axiom (xi after pi = pi' after xi', both auxiliaries shown to be isomorphisms).

Proposition prop-corr-zeta-pi, first sentence: for sharp s there exist a comprehension pi_s for s and a quotient zeta_s for s perp with zeta_s after pi_s = id and pi_s after zeta_s = asrt_s. Proof is the thesis's, including the identification im pi = s through diamond-self-adjointness of asrt_s.

Second sentence: for EVERY comprehension pi of s there is such a quotient. Ours strengthens "there is" to ExistsUnique, which is 211IX's "the unique quotient" - the doc comment says so, and uniqueness follows from monicity of pi. Proof is the thesis's transport along the iso relating two comprehensions.
Third sentence: conversely, for every quotient zeta for s perp there is a comprehension pi for s with the same two identities. Proof is the thesis's "proven in a similar way", spelled out.

Notation zeta-s-convention: the corresponding quotient zeta_s of the chosen comprehension pi_s, by unique choice from the previous row. Matches, and the Warning 211X (xi_{s perp} = zeta_s) is recorded in the doc comment.

Proposition upm-closed, first half: comprehensions are closed under composition. Stated as the existence of a predicate for which the composite is a comprehension, which is what "is a comprehension" means. Proof is the thesis's, including the s after zeta_2 >= im(pi_2 after pi_1) step.

Second half: pure maps are closed under composition. Proof is the thesis's - factor both, use the second andthen-effectus axiom on xi_1 after pi_2, then the previous half and 197IX quotients-composition.

Exercise andthen-square-rule: asrt_p after asrt_p = asrt_{p & p}. Proof is bsols.tex:3125 - the square is diamond-positive by 209III.3 with 211XI for purity, and 1 after it is p & p, so uniqueness of diamond-positive maps applies.

Exercise asrt-absorp-rule: both equivalences, im f <= s iff asrt_s after f = f, and 1 after f <= t iff f after asrt_t = f, for sharp s and t. Both are in the one theorem. Proof is bsols.tex:3134, using the corresponding pi/zeta pair in both directions.

Definition (eff.tex parsec 2110 point 160): the subcategory Pure C of pure maps. Rendered as a wrapper structure on objects with hom the pure maps; the category instance uses 211XI for composition and exhibits the identity as pure. Faithful to the definition, with the caveat that Pure C is a genuinely new type rather than a Mathlib subcategory - immaterial here.
Lemma zeta-asrt-quot: zeta_{ceil p} after asrt_p is a quotient for p perp. Proof is the thesis's - the image is 1, so in the pure factorisation the comprehension part is an isomorphism.

Proposition standard-form-map: every map factors as pi_{im f} after g after zeta_{ceil(1 after f)} after asrt_{1 after f} for a UNIQUE total and faithful g. Both the factorisation and the uniqueness are in the ExistsUnique, and the two properties of g are conjoined. Proof is the thesis's, including the faithfulness argument for g prime and the appeal to 197-quotient-total plus 212I.

Clause 1: if f is pure then the total faithful part g is an isomorphism. Stated for an arbitrary g satisfying the standard form (which by 212III is the g), which is the convenient form and is equivalent. Proof is the thesis's alpha-after-beta argument.

Clause 2: if f is pure and im f = 1 then f is a quotient. The hypothesis is FaithfulMap f, which is 202I.2's definition of im f = 1, so this is the point's hypothesis. Proof is the thesis's: pi_{im f} and g are both isomorphisms, and 212I supplies the quotient.
Clause 3: if f is pure and 1 after f = 1 then f is a comprehension. Proof is the thesis's "just as easy", spelled out: asrt_{1 after f} = id and zeta_{ceil(1 after f)} is an isomorphism.

Proposition andthen-effect-divisoid: (Scal C)op is an effect divisoid. Stated as Nonempty of the structure; since the division of an effect divisoid is pinned by its own uniqueness axiom, nothing is lost by not naming it. Proof is the thesis's: the division is lambda over mu = lambda prime after zeta_{ceil mu} built from 212I (helpers scalDiv, scal_factor), and all five axioms are checked as the thesis checks them.
